title: My Leni
primary_topics: Memorial biography of Professor Elenita 'Leni' Carpio-Panganiban (February 29, 1940 - April 9, 2023) -- CJP's wife of 62 years
Leni as a loving wife: from their 1958 train meeting to Naga City to 62nd wedding anniversary on April 8, 2023 -- one day before her sudden passing
Leni as a nurturing mother to five children: five eulogies quoted in full
Leni as an inspiring professor and colleague at AIM for 37 years (1973-2009), first woman on AIM faculty
sub_topics: Born February 29, 1940 (leap-year birthday); third among six children of Jose Agustin Carpio and Elena Navarro Alcazar

Education: Colegio de Jesus y Maria (1946-48), St. Scholastica's College (elementary 1948-51, high school with high honors 1951-55, BA and BS Education major Math cum laude 1959), MA Statistics UP Statistical Center 1963, MBA AIM 1971 (one of four women in pioneering mostly-male batch)
Central Bank career: 13 years as Senior Statistician, Supervising Statistician, then Economist; Central Bank granted her a full AIM scholarship

AIM career (1973-2009): first woman on AIM faculty; 37 years teaching MBM and MM programs; marketing management, quantitative analysis, advertising management; MBM Coordinator 1977-79, 1980-81, 1984-85; core MM faculty 1981-84; Associate Dean 1999-2000; adjunct faculty 2007-09
FLP Trustee; Supreme Court Ladies Circle President when CJP became CJ in 2005; Chairman of Baron Travel Corporation and Arpan Air (Royal Caribbean GSA); board member of AIMI and PPRC

Monsignor Gerry Santos's account of how they met: on a 1958 train to Naga City for an NUSP Seminar on Communism -- Art was NUSP president, Leni represented St. Scholastica's; Leni had wanted to be a Benedictine nun; they married April 8, 1961
2021 Diamond Anniversary: private celebration at Carmelite Chapel in Tagaytay, presided by Cardinal Advincula, attended by 86 incumbent archbishops and bishops of the Philippines
Final days: joyful visit to Singapore (April 1-7, 2023); couple privately celebrated 62nd anniversary April 8, 2023; Leni passed suddenly April 9, 2023

Five children's eulogies: Celine ('My Mom was my image of perfection... no greater love than a mother's love'); Len ('She was a constant, reassuring presence'); Archie (April 8 phone call: 'Mom seemed very happy and talkative... less than 24 hours later, she was gone'); Tet ('Tet, you are so quiet... You have to learn to fight' -- earliest significant lesson); Mabel (youngest: 'she made sure I felt loved, never forgotten... Mom put family above all else')
Dr. Jikyeong Kang (AIM President/Dean): 'smart, elegant, and beautiful yet soft-spoken and genteel'
Former VP Jejomar Binay letter (April 11, 2023): 'contributions to the academic and legal communities were significant'
Professor Tet Panganiban-Mañalac: 'My Mom was instrumental to my entry in AIM, where I now teach... I am my mother's daughter; a passionate teacher like her'
BLD Marriage Encounters: Art and Leni attended Marriage Encounter Seminar 1986 and Life in the Spirit Seminar; headed all BLD Marriage Encounters, became prayer leaders, headed BLD Foundation
Prof. Marirose Q. Sison-Garcia: 'Leni and CJ Art were serving as members of the Council of Servant Leaders... they introduced a joyful and animated format that brought new life to the BLD Community'
Fr. Robert Manansala homily: 'She was a most devoted daughter of God, who lived her faith in the Lord in her daily life in an exemplary manner'

stances.claim: Leni Panganiban was not a peripheral figure in CJP's career but its foundational inspiration -- 'the gentle wind beneath my wings.' Her 37 years at AIM, her Central Bank scholarship, her cum laude degree, and her founding role in the Supreme Court Ladies Circle demonstrate that she was an accomplished professional in her own right, not merely a supportive spouse.
stances.rhetorical_move: co-protagonist framing: Leni as an independent achiever, not just a supporting figure
stances.confidence: asserted through enumerated credentials and institutional roles

stances.claim: The last hours of Leni's life were a gift: the couple came back from a joyful Singapore trip (April 1-7), celebrated their 62nd anniversary in private on April 8, and Archie's phone call on April 8 found her 'very happy and talkative... she was giving us a gift to the very end.' She passed suddenly on April 9.
stances.rhetorical_move: providential-close-of-life narrative: the final hours as a farewell gift from a loving God

stances.claim: Leni's five children's eulogies constitute a coherent portrait of a woman who was simultaneously an 'image of perfection,' a constant reassuring presence, a fighter-in-chief (teaching Tet to fight), a devoted grandmother, and the 'heart and soul' of the family.
stances.rhetorical_move: multi-witness eulogy canon: five voices constructing one complete portrait
stances.confidence: asserted through direct quotation of all five children

2021 Diamond Anniversary: held privately at Carmelite Chapel, Tagaytay, presided by Cardinal Advincula and attended by all 86 incumbent archbishops and bishops of the Philippines.

Final Singapore trip and anniversary: joyful April 1-7, 2023 Singapore visit; private 62nd anniversary on April 8, 2023; Leni passed suddenly on April 9 -- 'That is so Mom, giving us a gift to the very end' (Archie's eulogy).
Tet's earliest lesson from Leni: when Tet was 14 and away on a high school retreat, Leni wrote her: 'Tet, you are so quiet... You have to learn to fight.'

one_paragraph_summary: Published April 9, 2023 -- the day of her passing -- this memorial biography of Professor Elenita 'Leni' Carpio-Panganiban, CJP's wife of 62 years, is structured in four sections: loving wife, nurturing mother, inspiring professor and colleague, and faithful daughter of God. Born on the leap-year date of February 29, 1940, she graduated cum laude from St. Scholastica's College, earned an MA in Statistics from UP's Statistical Center, and completed her MBA at AIM in 1971 as one of four women in the pioneering batch -- on a Central Bank full scholarship after 13 years as statistician and economist. She joined AIM's faculty in 1973 as its first woman faculty member and taught for 37 years (retiring 2009), serving as MBM Coordinator multiple terms and Associate Dean 1999-2000; her daughter Tet is now also an AIM professor. Msgr. Gerry Santos narrated their meeting: a 1958 train to Naga City for an NUSP Seminar on Communism (Art was NUSP president, Leni represented St. Scholastica's; she had wanted to be a Benedictine nun). They married April 8, 1961 at Immaculate Conception Parish Church in Cubao. The 2021 Diamond Anniversary was held privately at Carmelite Chapel, Tagaytay, presided by Cardinal Advincula and attended by all 86 incumbent Philippine archbishops and bishops. The couple returned from a joyful Singapore trip on April 7, 2023, privately celebrated their 62nd anniversary on April 8, and Leni passed suddenly on April 9 -- 'That is so Mom, giving us a gift to the very end' (Archie's eulogy). The biography quotes all five children: Celine ('My Mom was my image of perfection'); Len ('She was a constant, reassuring presence'); Archie (the April 8 phone call found her 'very happy and talkative... less than 24 hours later, she was gone'); Tet (Leni's letter: 'Tet, you are so quiet... You have to learn to fight'); and Mabel ('Mom put family above all else'). CJP calls her 'the gentle wind beneath my wings and the inspiration of my humble career.'
